prompts.lilt:
Edit this transparent 12-part human animation atlas. Keep the exact 3-column x4-row layout, same isolated body parts, same true transparency, same solid ultramarine #2455A4, no labels, no added pieces.
Refine the shapes so they feel like flowing Matisse cut paper, more graceful and less abrupt. The current upper arms and thighs have sudden hard changes in direction: replace these with long continuous tapered S-curves. Remove zig-zag corners in the middle of limbs. The outline should sweep naturally through elbow and knee shafts; joint bends will be animated later. Keep a few decisively cut flat edges at the shoulder tops, jaw edge, wrists and soles so it does not become bubbly. The forearms should be long tapering ribbons, hands loose and expressive with longer tapered scissor-cut fingers. Head: small tilted irregular oval with a gently angled jaw and short neck. Torso: fluid asymmetrical shoulders and long concave waist, hips formed by one shallow sweeping irregular arc, NO triangular zigzag crotch points. Keep the torso elongated. Feet simple long wedge silhouettes with smooth instep and short flat sole.
Think organic tension and effortless sweeping gesture. NOT round capsule mascot, NOT faceted cubist, NOT jagged or rigid. Less abrupt while retaining hand-cut irregularity. Flat untextured ink, no gradients, no speckle, no shadows. Keep all parts fully in their cells with generous empty gutters and clean alpha. One head, one torso/pelvis, two upper arms, two forearms/hands, two thighs, two shins/feet, two alternative open-hand forearms, same order as reference. Rounded little attachment caps may overlap behind adjoining parts in assembly.

prompts.lean:
Create a transparent 3-column 4-row character rig parts atlas, portrait, exactly twelve separate blue cut-paper body parts, one centered in each equal cell, no labels or grid.
Art direction: an original human inspired by Henri Matisse's Blue Nudes and The Dance, ACTUAL SCISSOR-CUT PAPER with long irregular sinuous contours. Body language lyrical, sensuous, spare, handmade. Strong taper, asymmetric curves, chisel-cut ends. A nuanced mix: approximately 70% long tense flowing convex and concave curves, 30% abrupt straight scissor cuts and pointed corners. Anatomical yet abstract. Slim elongated arms, strong irregular thighs, very simple head, elegantly asymmetric torso. Not soft rounded pill-shaped stock illustration; NOT angular robot, NOT faceted cubist polygons, NOT a geometric stickman. Important: do not build zig-zag limbs out of polygons. Each limb should have one continuous sweeping outside contour, one cut-in concave inside contour, with one or two sharp cut tips. Avoid repeated circular bulges.
Solid flat ultramarine #2455A4 ink, no outlines, no gradients, no texture, no shadows. Completely transparent background. Every piece separate, clean empty gutters. No full figure.
3 columns x4 rows. Reading order:
row1: 1 small tilted irregular oval HEAD with a straight clipped side and short neck pointing down; 2 elongated irregular TORSO INCLUDING PELVIS with diagonally cut shoulders, one sweeping concave waist side and an uneven angular pelvis edge, shoulders top; 3 LEFT UPPER ARM long tapered gently curved with shoulder top, elbow bottom.
row2: 1 LEFT FOREARM with flat integrated angular mitten hand bottom; 2 RIGHT UPPER ARM with shoulder top elbow bottom; 3 RIGHT FOREARM integrated angular mitten hand bottom.
row3: 1 LEFT THIGH strong tapered sweeping curve hip top knee bottom; 2 LEFT SHIN and integrated simple long wedge foot pointing left bottom, mostly straight outer shin and taut concave inner shin; 3 RIGHT THIGH hip top knee bottom.
row4: 1 RIGHT SHIN with foot pointing right bottom; 2 alternate LEFT FOREARM with expressive open long-fingered scissor-cut hand bottom; 3 alternate RIGHT FOREARM with expressive open hand bottom.
Joint ends only can have short round caps for overlapping behind other pieces, but the visible shafts must have organic tapered asymmetry with sharp details. Every segment almost vertical within cell. Torso about 175wide x300high, head100x140, upper arms45x230, forearms including hands55x235, thighs75x245, shins including feet80x260. Keep generous transparent gutters. All parts flat blue, one coherent original character named Lean. Make Lean distinct: a very slender torso with a diagonal shoulder line, a long narrow head with one straight jaw edge, elongated tapering thighs and forearms. Long continuous convex/concave scissor curves, mixed with straight cuts at knees and palms. Less wide than Lilt. Keep exact same 12-cell order; this is a production parts atlas.
